provenance.quote:
OFFICIAL TITLE: COUNTY JAILS: TRANSACTION PRIVILEGE TAX OF ONE-FIFTH OF ONE CENT, the same rate as the existing jail facilities excise tax expiring in March 2027. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: Pursuant to authority granted by the State of Arizona, the County seeks voter approval of a transaction privilege tax set at the rate allowed under A.R.S. § 42-6109.02, section A, one-ﬁfth of one cent to be used for county jail facilities and programs.
A "YES" vote shall have the effect of approving a sales tax of one-ﬁfth of one cent ($0.002) for county jail facilities and programs, the same rate as the current tax that is expiring.
A "NO" vote shall have the effect of rejecting a sales tax of one-ﬁfth of one cent ($0.002) for jail facilities and programs.

Shall the proposed Franchise Agreement, as published and submitted to the qualified electorate, be granted to Rose Valley Water Company, an Arizona corporation, to construct, maintain and operate water distribution and transmission systems in the City of Peoria, Arizona, and future annexations.
A "YES" vote will allow the City of Peoria to enter into the Franchise Agreement with Rose Valley Water Company.
A "NO" vote will deny the City of Peoria the authority to enter into the Franchise Agreement with Rose Valley Water Company.

OFFICIAL TITLE: A proposition submitted by the Tempe City Council, pursuant to the Tempe City Charter § 5.02, for a new transaction privilege (sales) tax and use tax, except for the privilege (sales) tax on food for home consumption, relating to public safety and security enhancements; public transit system and multimodal projects, including pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure; and Tempe early childhood care and preschool education. DESCRIPTIVE TITLE: Effective January 1, 2027, shall a new five-tenths of one percent (0.5%) transaction privilege (sales) tax and use tax, except for the privilege (sales) tax on food for home consumption, be levied and allocated as follows? 1) three-tenths of one percent (0.3%) to be designated to enhance public safety and strengthen the overall security of Tempe’s parks and neighborhoods, including funding for essential public safety infrastructure, operations, and services for police, fire, emergency operations, safety and security programs, and crime prevention through environmental design; 2) one-tenth of one percent (0.1%) to be designated for the improvement and operation of Tempe’s public transit system and multimodal projects, including pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure; and, 3) one-tenth of one percent (0.1%) to be designated to expand and strengthen early childhood care and preschool education and broaden access first to qualified Tempe residents, followed by teachers working in Tempe school districts, then to employees of the City of Tempe, and finally to non-residents who are employed by Tempe-based businesses. The City’s current tax rate, authorized by the voters, is 1.8 percent (1.2 percent General Fund, 0.5 percent Transit Tax, and 0.1 percent Arts & Culture Tax).
A “YES” vote shall have the effect of approving a new five-tenths of one percent (0.5%) transaction privilege (sales) tax and use tax, except for the privilege (sales) tax on food for home consumption, to enhance public safety and strengthen the overall security of Tempe’s parks, neighborhoods and public spaces; for the improvement and operation of Tempe’s public transit system and multimodal projects, including pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure; and expand and strengthen early childhood care and preschool education and broaden access first to qualified Tempe residents, followed by teachers working in Tempe school districts, then to employees of the City of Tempe, and finally to non-residents who are employed by Tempe-based businesses, effective January 1, 2027.
A “NO” vote shall have the effect of not approving a new five-tenths of one percent (0.5%) transaction privilege (sales) tax and use tax, except for the privilege (sales) tax on food for home consumption, to enhance public safety and strengthen the overall security of Tempe’s parks, neighborhoods and public spaces; for the improvement and operation of Tempe’s public transit system and multimodal projects, including pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure; and expand and strengthen early childhood care and preschool education and broaden access first to qualified Tempe residents, followed by teachers working in Tempe school districts, then to employees of the City of Tempe, and finally to non-residents who are employed by Tempe-based businesses, effective January 1, 2027.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces Maricopa County’s expiring jail tax with a sales tax at the same 0.2% rate, or 20 cents per $100 of taxable purchases, for up to 20 years. Collection starts the month after the existing tax expires in March 2027. Revenue is restricted to adult and juvenile jail buildings, operations and programs that reduce jail costs; the county may lower the rate during the term. County general-fund support for these facilities must also continue with annual inflation adjustments.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the replacement jail tax at the current rate for up to 20 years.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this replacement jail tax; the current tax is scheduled to expire in March 2027.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Gives Rose Valley Water Company a nonexclusive 25-year agreement to use Peoria’s public rights-of-way for water systems in its state-approved service area. The company must pay the city a franchise fee equal to 2% of its defined gross water-service receipts in Peoria and follow the agreement’s permitting, safety and other requirements. It takes effect on the first day of the month after voter approval. The company must provide the required service-area map and file written acceptance within 60 days after City Council approval.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Allow Peoria to enter the proposed water-utility franchise agreement with Rose Valley Water Company.
measureRecords.noMeans: Deny authority for Peoria to enter this proposed agreement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raises Tempe’s city sales and use tax from 1.8% to 2.3% beginning January 1, 2027, while food bought for home use stays at the current 1.8% sales-tax rate. The additional 0.5 percentage point is divided into 0.3 for public safety, 0.1 for transit and walking or cycling projects, and 0.1 for early childhood care and preschool. Child-care access is prioritized for qualified Tempe residents, then Tempe school-district teachers, city employees, and workers at Tempe-based businesses.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional 0.5% tax and its specified public-safety, transportation and early-childhood uses.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the city’s current 1.8% sales and use tax rate.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews Vail Unified School District’s authority to spend up to 12.5% above its state-set operating-budget limit for seven years, starting in 2027–28. Local property taxes would fund the renewal in addition to other district taxes. The legally required first-year estimate is $1.61 per $100 of assessed value using current-year property values; the district estimates about $1.55 using expected next-year values, subject to final values.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the existing operating-budget override and the property taxes that fund it.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not renew the override; the existing authorization is scheduled to shrink by one-third in each of 2027–28 and 2028–29.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews and increases Sahuarita Unified School District’s operating-budget override from 14% to 15% above the state-set limit. It runs for seven years starting in 2027–28: 15% for five years, then 10% and 5% in the final two years. Local property taxes would fund it at an estimated first-year rate of $1.31 per $100 of assessed value, in addition to other district taxes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the seven-year renewal and increase, funded by district property taxes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not renew or increase the override; the current 14% authorization is scheduled to phase down in 2028–29 and 2029–30 and end in 2030–31.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Renews Tanque Verde Unified School District’s authority to spend 15% above its state-set operating-budget limit for seven years, starting in 2027–28. The authority remains at 15% for five years, then drops to 10% and 5% in the last two years. Local property taxes would fund it at an estimated first-year rate of $0.88 per $100 of assessed value, in addition to other district taxes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Renew the existing operating-budget override and the property taxes that fund it.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not renew the override; the current authorization is scheduled to phase down in 2028–29 and 2029–30 and end in 2030–31.
